content: To overcome this difficulty, we propose to decouple the objective of learning a neural representation of conversational dynamics from the objective of predicting future events. The former can be pre-trained on large amounts of unsupervised data, similarly to how chatbots are trained. The latter can piggy-back on the resulting representation after fine-tuning it for classification using relatively small labeled data. While similar pre-train-then-fine-tune approaches have recently achieved state-of-the-art performance in a number of NLP tasks—including natural language inference, question answering, and commonsense reasoning (discussed in Section SECREF2)—to the best of our knowledge this is the first attempt at applying this paradigm to conversational forecasting.
